reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 describes a fracture toughness test method but provides no data on nano-twins or the target alloy. E2 mentions nano-twinned polycrystalline specimens in a nanoimprinting context, unrelated to the alloy or caloric properties. E3 shows that interstitial elements can increase stacking fault energy and suppress twinning, which conflicts with the premise of inducing nano-twins via annealing. No evidence supports the claim that the caloric transition is insensitive to twin boundaries.
premises: Nano-twins act as barriers to dislocation motion and crack propagation, improving toughness and ductility.
The order-disorder transition responsible for the caloric response is governed by bulk atomic rearrangements, not fine-scale twin boundaries.
Post-deformation annealing can induce a refined, nano-twinned grain structure in the alloy.
The proposed treatment will preserve at least 90% of the original caloric entropy change.
